subject: Phase 100120: intent gate, hybrid retrieve, and compose_context (clio-retrieve)
verdict_justification: The new clio-retrieve crate is well-structured and almost every phase acceptance criterion is backed by a real, passing test; I independently reran the full suite (487 passed), clippy, fmt, per-file coverage (all >=90%), and the opt-in Postgres parity test and they hold. The weaknesses are honesty/process rather than runtime correctness: the Definition of Done marks independent approval and verification as complete while the sign-off rows are still pending, one phase Expected Result (hybrid beats dense-only/lexical-only on a labeled fixture, with a documented metric) has no evidence, and retrieve can exceed its optional budget for a single oversized hit.

issues.title: Definition of Done overclaims independent approval and verification
issues.why_it_matters: The DoD is the phase's completion contract; checking 'Required approval is obtained' and 'Verification is completed' before the adversary and human approve turns an unverified state into a claimed one, which is the exact failure mode the review pipeline exists to prevent.
issues.impact: Pipeline and human reviewers may treat phase 100120 as approved when only the developer's self-check has happened.
issues.proposed_fix: Uncheck 'Verification is completed' and 'Required approval is obtained' until the adversary/human rows complete; or relabel them as 'self-verification completed; independent verification pending'.

issues.title: retrieve() can exceed its requested budget_tokens for a single oversized hit
issues.why_it_matters: Task 4 requires retrieve to honor budgets when trimming the returned pack. The `&& !hits.is_empty()` guard means the first candidate is admitted even when it alone is larger than the budget, so the optional budget is a soft floor, not a cap.
issues.impact: A caller passing a small budget_tokens can receive a hit whose estimated_tokens exceeds it. The PR-1 injection bound is still safe because compose re-truncates in pack_memory (compose.rs:289-316), so this is a retrieve-contract issue, not an injection leak.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-retrieve/src/finalize.rs:50-55: `if let Some(budget) = args.req.budget_tokens && estimated_tokens + tokens > budget && !hits.is_empty() { break; }`. No test exercises a single hit larger than the budget (budget_tokens_trims_returned_hits uses two 8-token hits with budget 8).
issues.proposed_fix: Either drop/skip a candidate that alone exceeds the remaining budget, or explicitly document and test that at least one hit is always returned as a deliberate behavior with its budget consequence stated.

issues.title: Phase Task 2 Expected Result ('hybrid beats dense-only and lexical-only on a labeled fixture, document metric') has no evidence
issues.why_it_matters: The phase states this as the outcome that proves Task 2. AC-100120-04 only checks that a lexical-only exact hit is included; it does not measure any quality lift, so the substantive claim about hybrid retrieval is unverified.
issues.impact: Phase 100120 is accepted without demonstrating the core value proposition of hybrid retrieval; a regression that drops lexical recall below dense-only would still pass every test.
issues.evidence: hybrid_tests.rs:40-63 (t06 asserts only membership of the lexical-only hit plus candidate counts); no fixture computes a dense-only or lexical-only baseline. grep across *_tests.rs for 'dense-only|lexical-only|metric' finds no comparison.
issues.proposed_fix: Add a small labeled fixture with a documented metric (e.g. recall@k or MRR) and assert hybrid >= dense-only and hybrid >= lexical-only, or downgrade the phase Expected Result to match what is actually tested.

issues.title: Seven new test source files omit the AGENTS.md-mandated header structure
issues.why_it_matters: AGENTS.md states every Rust source file MUST use the Responsibility / Owns / Does not own / Boundary header. Test files are Rust source files.
issues.impact: Rule non-compliance across seven files; inconsistent documentation conventions for the new crate.
issues.evidence: intent_tests.rs:1-4, compose_tests.rs:1-4, hybrid_tests.rs:1-4, surface_tests.rs:1-4, fusion_tests.rs:1-4, filter_tests.rs:1-4, rerank_tests.rs:1-4 each have only copyright + SPDX + one-line //! doc. fixtures_tests.rs:1-18 and pg_parity_tests.rs:1-20 have the full structure.
issues.proposed_fix: Add the full header block to the seven test files.

issues.title: section 8 normative false-negative tracking is reduced to a generic skip counter
issues.why_it_matters: requirement.md:681 says the intent gate's false-negative rate SHALL be tracked separately from, and held to a stricter bound than, its false-positive rate. evaluated/skipped counters cannot express either rate because there is no ground truth attached to a decision.
issues.impact: The system cannot currently demonstrate the stricter false-negative bound the spec demands; a gate that skips many memory-needed turns looks identical to a well-calibrated one in metrics.
issues.evidence: intent.rs:90-123 (GateMetrics: evaluated, skipped only); intent_tests.rs:108-116 asserts only those two counters. No false_negative/false_positive symbol exists anywhere in crates/.
issues.proposed_fix: Add a labeled evaluation hook that records expected_needed vs decision (FN/FP counters) and a documented stricter FN bound, or explicitly scope this metric to a later offline-evaluation phase and say so in the phase file.

issues.title: Nothing is staged, contradicting the review premise that the developer staged the changes
issues.why_it_matters: The reviewer instructions say to review `git diff --cached`; that diff is empty, and the new crate is entirely untracked. The developer's own log states they deliberately skipped git add due to a global rule, so the intended pipeline step cannot run as specified.
issues.impact: Automated review of the staged diff sees no code; the changes could be missed or duplicated if the pipeline stages later.
issues.evidence: `git diff --cached -- . ':!.workflows/'` -> empty. `git diff --stat` shows 7 tracked files; `git ls-files --others` lists 21 untracked files under crates/clio-retrieve/. Developer log line: 'did not run git add ... changes are unstaged'.
issues.proposed_fix: Pipeline (or user) stages with the documented pathspec, or the conflict between the global no-git rule and the developer-task staging instruction is resolved explicitly.

issues.title: clio-retrieve's in-process tool schema requires `bank`, which is absent from the published section 4.9.4.B signature
issues.why_it_matters: requirement.md:342-344 and phase Task 4 list retrieve(query, domains?, limit?, as_of?, time_axis?, expand_graph?, budget_tokens?) and compose_context(query?, domains?, budget_tokens) with no bank argument. The schema adds a required bank.
issues.impact: Slices 100160-17 MCP binding must invent a bank-injection convention or change the schema; a generated tool catalog from the requirement would not match the implementation.
issues.evidence: surface.rs:50-53 (RetrieveArgs.bank required) and surface.rs:77-79 + 165-170 (ComposeArgs.bank optional then rejected if missing).
issues.proposed_fix: Document that bank is supplied by the transport/session binding and make it explicit in the phase evidence, or align the argument contract with the requirement.

issues.title: Retrieve and compose measure different text when applying the same token budget
issues.why_it_matters: finalize measures lexical/book text; compose measures the hit's gist (or snapshot ref / id). The same hit has two different token costs, so retrieve's budget trimming can be much more aggressive than the memory section needs, and estimated_tokens in RetrieveOutcome does not describe the composed pack.
issues.impact: Under-filled memory sections and a metric (estimated_tokens) whose meaning differs between retrieve and compose; both remain bounded, so no injection overrun.
issues.evidence: finalize.rs:49 uses doc_text(Some(item)) = clio_index::lexical_text (hybrid.rs:419-421). compose.rs:289-326 pack_memory uses hit_text = gist | snapshot_ref | item_id (compose.rs:318-326).
issues.proposed_fix: Pick one canonical budgeted representation, or document the two and report both sizes.

issues.title: T100120-03 latency test cannot fail on any realistic machine and is presented as NFR-1 evidence
issues.why_it_matters: The gate runs in-memory with no I/O; a p95 threshold of 50,000 microseconds over 2000 calls is trivially met, so the test is a smoke test rather than a bound. Labelling it as satisfying NFR-1 overstates the evidence.
issues.impact: A future change that adds real work to the gate (e.g. a classifier call) could still pass this test up to ~50 ms per call.
issues.evidence: intent_tests.rs:91-106: samples 2000 gate calls per microsecond clock, asserts p95 <= 50_000 us. The gate itself (intent.rs:127-171) does only string ops.
issues.proposed_fix: State in the phase file that this is a smoke check and that the real NFR-1 guard is the absence of I/O in the gate; optionally add a tighter sanity bound (e.g. <1 ms) plus a structural test that the gate has no embedder/graph dependency.

issues.title: graph_expanded metric counts candidates that were already returned by dense/lexical legs
issues.why_it_matters: The metric is meant to report how many genuinely graph-expanded candidates entered the result set; counting ids that were already candidates overstates graph contribution and will mislead slice 100130 tuning.
issues.impact: Diagnostic only; no ranking or budget impact.
issues.evidence: hybrid.rs:164: `let graph_expanded = fused.iter().filter(|h| expanded.contains(&h.id)).count();` — `expanded` ids are appended to candidate_ids (hybrid.rs:151-155) but an id present in both lists is still counted.
issues.proposed_fix: Count only expanded ids that were absent from the dense and lexical filtered lists.

strengths: Weighted RRF is implemented exactly as documented and reduced to classic Cormack RRF when weights are 1; the appendix tie discrepancy is documented and tested against the formula.
Fail-open behavior is real and tested three ways (failing reranker, dead HTTP sidecar, malformed response) and dense-leg outages degrade to lexical-only with structured warnings.
Bank isolation, bi-temporal filtering, and domain filtering are enforced on every path and covered by adversarial tests.
Compose dual-budget packing is genuinely bounded across budgets from 9 to 2048 tokens, and the persona channel is emitted even on the auto-skip path.
Independent verification replicates every headline claim: 487 tests, clean clippy/fmt, 98.55/98.87 coverage with no file below 90%, and a passing Postgres parity run.
Production code has no unwrap/expect/panic, forbids unsafe, and keeps every file under the 450-line cap.
regrets: The review could not inspect a staged diff because nothing was staged; I derived staged-vs-unstaged from git diff variants instead of git status (global rule).
I could not construct a runtime counterexample for the retrieve budget overrun without editing the repository, so finding 2 rests on code inspection of finalize.rs.
